topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Key Strategy
explanation: Caching is the core strategy used within the memory hierarchy to mitigate the significant speed disparity between the CPU and main memory (DRAM). This mechanism exploits temporal and spatial locality by storing frequently accessed blocks of main memory data in smaller, faster cache levels (L1, L2, L3) proximate to the processor. The objective is to maximize the cache hit rate, ensuring that data requests are satisfied by the fastest memory tier. Successful cache utilization directly minimizes the Average Memory Access Time (AMAT), which is critical for high instruction execution throughput.
